summary: The identifier gate reads git objects, commit messages and the working tree instead of the index, so it can finally see the incident it was written for — a blob that survived `git rm`.
details: The previous version walked `git ls-files`. The incident it documents is a blob that stayed reachable after the file was deleted, and an index cannot see one: replaying it exactly — add corpus, commit, `git rm`, commit — left the gate green with eleven thousand real fixes reachable from HEAD~1. It never read commit messages either, though identifiers demonstrably reach them.

It failed OPEN four ways, each a silent `continue`: one appended non-UTF-8 byte, a `.svg` rename, a symlink, a UTF-16 encoding. Undecodable content and non-regular tracked paths are now ERRORS with a declared allowlist, and there is no suffix skip list at all.

The working tree is scanned alongside objects. Objects are what would be published; the working tree is what is about to become one. Found by attacking this change: four planted payloads went undetected while uncommitted and all four failed the moment they were committed — a capability the index-reading version had and this one would otherwise have lost.

Values are normalised before matching, so a separator-formatted number and a dashless or upper-case UUID collapse to their declared form. The coordinate rule is shape-agnostic across comma-, tab- and JSON-separated rows.

A location table must now be declared WITH A SIZE. Exempting a path outright — the previous form — let the next corpus be pasted into a file already on the list, which is the same disclosure by a shorter route. Historical blobs carrying location data are pinned by blob sha as #167's burn-down list, so the scrub removing them makes the pins stale and the stale-pin test fails until they are deleted.

Nothing is exempt by path any more, including the gate's own source — the one file an auditor previously found four real identifiers in, and a path exemption is forgeable besides. Scanning itself immediately caught an undeclared value in its own docstring.

Threshold set by measurement rather than convenience: across all history the incident corpus holds 17,200 such numbers and the next largest blob holds 40. 12 sits BELOW the smallest real table in the repo (design/proposed/27 at 22) rather than above the largest fixture, because the question is what payload does harm.

Annotated TAG messages are scanned. `rev-list --objects --all` lists tag objects but the batch reader keeps only blobs and `git log` never prints them, so three existing tags were read by nothing while `git push --tags` publishes them.

A trailing full stop no longer hides a platform id (`guild 1499876543210987654.` was invisible), a bare `852`-prefixed number and its WhatsApp JID form are detected, and lookalike separators are folded — a single non-breaking space inside a phone number defeated the whole detector while rendering identically on screen.
The walk-size check moved INSIDE the fixture as a precondition. As a sibling test it could be deselected while every content test passed against an empty corpus.

`_PENDING_REAL_UUIDS`, `_PENDING_REAL_IPS` and `_PENDING_REAL_NAMES` were declared and checked by nothing. Private addresses are now scanned, and every burn-down value must still be present or be deleted from the list.

Coordinates are counted per COMMIT AND TAG MESSAGE as well as per blob, each message on its own — the coordinate test read blobs only, so a table pasted into a commit message was invisible while a phone number beside it was caught. Counting the concatenation instead would be meaningless: a dozen coordinates spread over two thousand commits is not a table.
limitations: The `_PENDING_REAL_*` inventories still hold real identifiers, deliberately. This repository is private and still carries what it carried before the scrub; the lists only shrink, and the published copy has them empty by construction. Nothing in them may be copied into a public tree.

The name half remains a regression pin, not a detector. There is no allowlist over English, so it stops the eight names already present from spreading and cannot catch the next one. A green run is not 'no real names in the tree'.
Runtime is ~26s against ~9,300 objects, up from ~1.4s. That is the cost of reading objects rather than the index.

Runtime is ~107s against ~22,000 objects, down from 150s once every detector was made to run once per blob rather than once per test, and up from 1.4s for the index-reading version. Reading objects is what costs; skipping lockfiles to go faster would reopen the suffix hole this change closed.

The coordinate rule counts decimal LITERALS, which measures neither dimension of the harm. Measured on one 400-fix trace: 800 literals as plain decimals, and ZERO as int-scaled microdegrees, comma decimals, two-decimal precision, an offset past `\d{1,3}`, integer+fraction columns, DMS, geohash or Plus Codes. Two thousand rows across two locations is four literals. It catches a corpus pasted as it came out of the database — how the one real incident happened — and nothing cleverer. #182 has the measurements and what a real detector needs.

Declared table CONTENT is unconstrained: sizes are pinned at their maxima so growth is blocked, but swapping every coordinate in a declared file for a different one keeps the count and stays green (#182).
Declarations are still attacker-writable in the same change, and because the gate now scans its own source the stale-check is satisfied by the declaration literal itself (#182).
